WHY A NEW TERM AND NOT THE BALLSEC WEIGHT, settled by measurement before anything was written. Moving weight from volume (0.26) to ballsec (0.10) charges the subject 38 points of gap per unit of weight — but it charges James Harden '19 FORTY-THREE (volume 99, ball security 56), so his 95 +-1 pin breaks before the subject has moved four. The global dial cannot separate them; only a term that also reads efficiency can. That is the same wall recal_91, recal_98 and recal_112 hit on the efficiency weight, on the neighbouring bar.

THE RE-CUT IS THE SMALLEST ONE THAT DOES THE JOB, and three were measured. (a) efficiency 51 -> 60, the class's lower tercile to its median: K stays 6.3 because the subject sits AT the new floor, 35 cards move, 103 printed points shed, max -6 — SHIPPED. (b) 46 -> 60, its lower QUARTILE to the median: spares the same two men but K must rise to 9.8, and the ceiling with it — 39 cards, 148 points, max -9, Westbrook '18 to 75 and '19 to 70. Rejected: it buys nothing and deepens the tail. (c) 54 -> 60, which would put the SUBJECT inside the leg rather than at its floor: it BREAKS the round's own order pin, because Westbrook '17 (48) and '15 (51) then take the same full efficiency gate and '17 finishes ABOVE '15, 87 to 86. The floor of the leg has to sit at or below the subject, and the highest quantile that does is the lower tercile.

WHY THE TERM IS GATED ON HANDLING LOAD AND NOT ON VOLUME ALONE, and this is the load-bearing choice. His sentence is about a man with the ball in his hands — usage AND creation. Read on volume alone, Jaylen Brown '26 (96) sits at three-quarters of the gate and drifts to 82; read on the mean of volume and playvol, he is 82 and OUTSIDE it, because he does not create. Westbrook '15 is 95.5. It also disposes of the whole low-creation half of the board for free: Kobe '16 (79.5) and Carmelo '13 (73.5) never reach the gate at all, on top of their ball security already ending it.

WHAT MAKES THIS NARROW WHERE recal_85's TAX WAS NOT, stated because his own ruling deleted that tax and recal_111 refused this ruling on exactly that ground. Three differences, all structural. (1) POSITION: the tax lived in the OVR core, AFTER o_ovr and d_ovr were fixed, and subtracted from the blend — which is why it made 192 cards print BELOW their weaker end. This charge is inside o_score, so what falls is OFF itself and the blend still reads between a card's two ends; no card can print below its weaker end from it, by construction. (2) SHAPE: the tax read heavy load at poor efficiency, one fault. This needs BOTH, and the second is what spares the Kobe/Iverson/Carmelo class the ruling does not name. (3) SIZE: 48 cards move, against the tax's 192, and every one of them is a high-usage creator who neither converts nor keeps the ball.

EVERY CONSTANT IS A QUANTILE OF THE CLASS OR A MEASURED FRONTIER, none is taste. Of the 218 cards at handling load >= 85: efficiency median 60 and upper quartile 76 (the leg runs 60 -> 75); ball-security lower quartile 58 (the leg is full at 58 and below). The subject sits at the class's 33rd percentile of efficiency and its 32nd of ball security — poor at both, which is the whole claim. The ball-security leg's TOP, 65, is a frontier rather than a quantile: a WIDER fade needs a SMALLER size for the same subject and therefore leaves a shallower tail, so the round takes the widest fade the ordering permits, and at 66 the term can no longer put Westbrook '17 at or below '15.

REJECTED (a): reading the charge off efficiency ALONE, at any size. Jaylen Brown '26 is efficiency 38 against the subject's 51, so every such charge reaches HIM harder — this is recal_111's proof and it survives untouched. Rejected (b): the ball-security leg alone, at any size — James Harden '19 is ball security 56 against the subject's 60 and would break first, and Harden '17 (46) and '18 (53) with him. The two legs are only defensible multiplied.

REJECTED (c), and it is worth naming because it looked cheapest: a steeper VOLUME gate (90 -> 98) instead of the handling gate. It reaches the number and holds every anchor, but it puts Jaylen Brown '26 on 82 — inside his tolerance by one point and for no reason his ruling gives, since Brown's fault is conversion, not the ball. The handling gate leaves him at 83, exactly where recal_89 put him.

MEASURED, AND THE LAB REPRODUCES THE SHIPPED BOARD TO ZERO MISMATCHES ON ALL 10,000 CARDS BEFORE ANY CHANGE WAS APPLIED, so every number here is a reading of the real pipeline rather than a model of it.

WHO TAKES THE WHOLE CHARGE NOW, asked because a narrower leg usually needs a bigger size: nobody new. K is still 6.3 and it is still the ceiling — the full charge needs handling load >= 95, efficiency <= 51 AND ball security <= 58, which is Westbrook '17 and Westbrook '18 (handling load 98.5 and 98.0). No card on the board loses more than six printed points, exactly as before the amendment.
